chunk_findings.detail: The change ships a regression test but no fix. The new test asserts that `pairs._settled(st, "B1", "fix-B1")` and `pairs._settled(st, "fix-B1", "B1")` are true after `bug found --id B1` auto-files `fix-B1`. Per the change's own description, on the current (unfixed) code each bug/fix-task pair "shows up as an unsettled pair at the ask threshold", i.e. `_settled` returns false for exactly this input — which is why the intent says to "watch it FAIL on the unfixed code". Since the diff contains no non-test file, nothing in this change makes that assertion pass: the pair-filtering/`_settled` logic is untouched, so running the suite after this change yields a red test while the reported symptom (`ddflow dupes --limit 0` listing `Bfb0bc80b61 ~ fix-Bfb0bc80b61`) remains. To be a valid change it must also carry the production edit that makes a derived companion pair considered settled; as submitted, the bug is not fixed and the test suite is left failing.

chunk_findings.detail: The negative guard asserts `not P._settled(st, "B1", "B2")`, but this test never creates B2: it only runs `init` and a single `bug found --id B1` (line 144) before loading state. So B2 is absent from the store, and `_settled` will return False for that pair simply because one side is unknown/nonexistent — not because the derived-companion rule is correctly scoped to linked pairs. The assertion therefore passes for the wrong reason and gives false assurance that two genuinely unrelated bugs remain unsettled; if `_settled` were later changed to return False for any missing id, this line would still pass while the rule over-settles real pairs. The sibling test `test_a_related_link_also_settles_the_pair` builds both ids via `_two_bugs(repo)`; creating B2 (or reusing that helper) is required for the check to mean anything.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated purpose of this change is to fix B623baa4359 — "dupes offers a bug and its own auto-filed fix task as a possible duplicate" — but the diff contains no production-code change at all: `part 1 of 1` shows a single inserted line in a test file, `run_cli(repo, "bug", "found", "--id", "B2", "--summary", BUG_B, "--no-task")`. Nothing in the dupes offer/sweep logic is touched, so the pair-ranking code that emitted `0.94 Bfb0bc80b61 ~ fix-Bfb0bc80b61` still behaves exactly as before. Concretely: run `ddflow dupes --limit 0` on a repo containing one bug created without `--no-task` (i.e. with its auto-filed fix task) and the bug/fix pair is still offered at the ask threshold, which is precisely the repro in the intent. Because the only thing added is test scaffolding, either (a) the new test does reproduce the reported condition and now fails in CI (no fix accompanied it), or (b) it does not reproduce it, in which case it is not a valid regression test and the bug cannot be closed against it — the project's workflow enforcement makes "must have regression test" a hard constraint, and a test that does not fail on the unfixed code does not satisfy it [D-rules-hierarchy]. Note also that the new line explicitly passes `--no-task` for B2, i.e. it suppresses auto-task filing for that bug, so at most B1 can supply the bug/own-fix-task pair the change is supposed to guard; if the assertion block below (unchanged by this diff) keys off B2, the scenario under test is not the reported one at all.
